paragraphs.title: Joseph Brings His Sons to His Sick Father Jacob

easy.question: Who was sick at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Jacob
Joseph
Manasseh
easy.explanation: Joseph heard that his father Jacob was sick.

easy.question: Whom did Joseph take with him?
answers: His brothers
His two sons
His father's servants
easy.explanation: Joseph took Manasseh and Ephraim, his two sons, with him.

easy.question: What did Jacob do when Joseph came to him?
answers: He left the house
He went to sleep
He sat up on the bed
easy.explanation: When Joseph arrived, Jacob strengthened himself and sat on the bed.

medium.question: Why did Joseph take Manasseh and Ephraim with him?
answers: Because his father was sick, and he came with his sons
Because they were soldiers
Because they were looking for Jacob
medium.explanation: Joseph heard that his father was sick, so he came to him with his two sons.

medium.question: What does the phrase “Israel strengthened himself” mean in this context?
answers: He fell asleep
He gathered his strength and made an effort
He became angry
medium.explanation: Jacob was sick, but when Joseph came, he gathered his strength and sat on the bed.

medium.question: What happened first?
answers: Jacob sat on the bed
Joseph took his sons
Jacob blessed his sons
medium.explanation: First Joseph took Manasseh and Ephraim; only afterward was Jacob told that Joseph was coming.

challenge.question: Why are both “Jacob” and “Israel” used in these verses?
answers: They were two different people
They were two names for the same person
One of them was Joseph’s son
challenge.explanation: Jacob and Israel are two names for the same person, Joseph’s father.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Jacob strengthening himself and sitting on the bed?
answers: He prepared to receive Joseph despite his weakness
He was no longer sick
He wanted to begin a journey
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Jacob was sick, so his strengthening himself shows that he made an effort to receive Joseph.

challenge.question: Who told Jacob that Joseph was coming to him?
answers: Manasseh
One of Jacob’s servants
Someone not identified in the verse
challenge.explanation: The verse only says, “Someone told Jacob,” without identifying the messenger.

questions.question: Why are both “Jacob” and “Israel” used in these verses?
answers: They were two different people
They were two names for the same person
One of them was Joseph’s son
questions.explanation: Jacob and Israel are two names for the same person, Joseph’s father.

questions.question: What can we infer from Jacob strengthening himself and sitting on the bed?
answers: He prepared to receive Joseph despite his weakness
He was no longer sick
He wanted to begin a journey
questions.explanation: The passage says that Jacob was sick, so his strengthening himself shows that he made an effort to receive Joseph.

questions.question: Who told Jacob that Joseph was coming to him?
answers: Manasseh
One of Jacob’s servants
Someone not identified in the verse
questions.explanation: The verse only says, “Someone told Jacob,” without identifying the messenger.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Tells Joseph About God’s Blessing and the Promise of the Land

easy.question: Where did God appear to Jacob?
answers: At Luz in the land of Canaan
In Egypt
At Bethlehem
easy.explanation: Jacob said that God appeared to him at Luz in the land of Canaan.

easy.question: Who were Joseph’s two sons born in Egypt?
answers: Reuben and Simeon
Ephraim and Manasseh
Judah and Levi
easy.explanation: The passage names Joseph’s two sons born in Egypt as Ephraim and Manasseh.

easy.question: Where was Rachel buried?
answers: At Luz
In Egypt
On the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem
easy.explanation: Jacob said that Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.

medium.question: Why did Jacob count Ephraim and Manasseh as Reuben and Simeon?
answers: Because they were his firstborn sons
So they would have the status and inheritance of his own sons
Because they were born in Canaan
medium.explanation: Jacob adopted Ephraim and Manasseh as sons with independent status, like Reuben and Simeon.

medium.question: What does the phrase “an everlasting possession” mean in this context?
answers: A long journey
A temporary blessing
A permanent inheritance or possession
medium.explanation: The context concerns the land given forever to Jacob’s descendants, so it means a permanent inheritance.

medium.question: What would happen to Joseph’s additional children born after Ephraim and Manasseh?
answers: They would be counted under their brothers’ inheritance
They would not be considered part of Joseph’s family
They would receive the land of Canaan by themselves
medium.explanation: Jacob said that Joseph’s later children would be called after their brothers in their inheritance.

challenge.question: What was the practical meaning of Ephraim and Manasseh being counted like Reuben and Simeon?
answers: Each would have the importance of a separate tribe
They would return to live in Egypt
They would be younger than Reuben and Simeon
challenge.explanation: Comparing them to Reuben and Simeon shows that Ephraim and Manasseh would have independent status among Israel’s tribes.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the phrase “when there was but a little way to come unto Ephrath” about Rachel’s death?
answers: Rachel died after reaching Ephrath
Rachel died before reaching Ephrath, a short distance away
Rachel died in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that Rachel died while the family was still some distance from its destination.

challenge.question: Which detail identifies Ephrath with a more familiar place?
answers: Ephrath is identified with Luz
Ephrath is identified with Egypt
Ephrath is identified with Bethlehem
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “the same is Bethlehem,” identifying Ephrath with Bethlehem.

questions.question: What was the practical meaning of Ephraim and Manasseh being counted like Reuben and Simeon?
answers: Each would have the importance of a separate tribe
They would return to live in Egypt
They would be younger than Reuben and Simeon
questions.explanation: Comparing them to Reuben and Simeon shows that Ephraim and Manasseh would have independent status among Israel’s tribes.

questions.question: What can we understand from the phrase “when there was but a little way to come unto Ephrath” about Rachel’s death?
answers: Rachel died after reaching Ephrath
Rachel died before reaching Ephrath, a short distance away
Rachel died in Egypt
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that Rachel died while the family was still some distance from its destination.

questions.question: Which detail identifies Ephrath with a more familiar place?
answers: Ephrath is identified with Luz
Ephrath is identified with Egypt
Ephrath is identified with Bethlehem
questions.explanation: The verse says, “the same is Bethlehem,” identifying Ephrath with Bethlehem.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Meets and Blesses Joseph’s Sons

easy.question: Who asked, “Who are these?”
answers: Israel
Joseph
Ephraim
easy.explanation: Israel saw Joseph’s sons and asked who they were.

easy.question: What were Joseph’s sons, according to Joseph?
answers: His servants
His sons
His brothers
easy.explanation: Joseph told Israel, “They are my sons.”

easy.question: What did Israel do to Joseph’s sons?
answers: He blessed them immediately
He sent them to Egypt
He kissed and embraced them
easy.explanation: After Joseph brought them near, Israel kissed and embraced them.

medium.question: Why could Israel not see clearly?
answers: Because he was old
Because he was sick
Because he was far away from them
medium.explanation: The verse says that Israel’s eyes were dim because of old age.

medium.question: What did Joseph do after saying that they were his sons?
answers: He took them out of the room
He asked that they be brought near so Israel could bless them
He sent them to their brothers
medium.explanation: Joseph said, “Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them.”

medium.question: What does the phrase “his eyes were dim for age” mean?
answers: His eyes became larger
His eyes became beautiful
His eyesight had become weak
medium.explanation: The context says Israel could not see, so the phrase means that his eyesight had grown weak.

challenge.question: What did Israel mean by “I had not thought to see thy face”?
answers: I did not expect to see you again
I did not want to see you
I did not recognize your face
challenge.explanation: Israel expressed surprise and joy that he had been able to see Joseph again.

challenge.question: What did Joseph do immediately after bringing his sons out from between Israel’s knees?
answers: He brought them back to himself
He bowed before Israel with his face to the ground
He called for his brothers
challenge.explanation: After bringing them out, Joseph bowed himself before his father.

challenge.question: To whom did Israel give credit for allowing him to see both Joseph and Joseph’s descendants?
answers: Joseph
Joseph’s sons
God
challenge.explanation: Israel said, “God hath shewed me also thy seed,” giving God the credit.

questions.question: What did Israel mean by “I had not thought to see thy face”?
answers: I did not expect to see you again
I did not want to see you
I did not recognize your face
questions.explanation: Israel expressed surprise and joy that he had been able to see Joseph again.

questions.question: What did Joseph do immediately after bringing his sons out from between Israel’s knees?
answers: He brought them back to himself
He bowed before Israel with his face to the ground
He called for his brothers
questions.explanation: After bringing them out, Joseph bowed himself before his father.

questions.question: To whom did Israel give credit for allowing him to see both Joseph and Joseph’s descendants?
answers: Joseph
Joseph’s sons
God
questions.explanation: Israel said, “God hath shewed me also thy seed,” giving God the credit.

paragraphs.title: Joseph Arranges His Sons Before the Blessing

easy.question: Who placed his hands on Ephraim and Manasseh’s heads?
answers: Israel
Joseph
Isaac
easy.explanation: Israel stretched out his hands, placing his right hand on Ephraim and his left hand on Manasseh.

easy.question: Who was younger among the two sons?
answers: Manasseh
Ephraim
Joseph
easy.explanation: The verse says of Ephraim, “he was the younger.”

easy.question: Who were the two young men whom Israel blessed?
answers: Abraham and Isaac
Joseph and Benjamin
Ephraim and Manasseh
easy.explanation: Israel blessed Ephraim and Manasseh, Joseph’s sons.

medium.question: What did Joseph do by placing Ephraim in his right hand and Manasseh in his left?
answers: He arranged them in the opposite order from their birth order
He raised both of his hands
He folded his hands
medium.explanation: Joseph placed the older son, Manasseh, toward Israel’s right hand and the younger son, Ephraim, toward his left.

medium.question: Why did Joseph place Ephraim toward Israel’s left hand and Manasseh toward his right?
answers: Because Ephraim was the firstborn
Because Manasseh was the firstborn and Joseph wanted him to receive the right hand
Because Ephraim was taller
medium.explanation: Joseph knew Manasseh was the firstborn and wanted him to receive the more honored right hand.

medium.question: What did Israel ask to happen to Ephraim and Manasseh?
answers: That they return to Egypt
That they rule Joseph’s family
That God’s name and the names of Abraham and Isaac be invoked over them, and that they multiply greatly
medium.explanation: Israel asked that his name and the names of Abraham and Isaac be named on them and that they grow into a multitude.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Israel placing his right hand on the younger Ephraim?
answers: The greater blessing was given to the younger, although Manasseh was firstborn
Ephraim was Manasseh’s father
Israel did not know who was firstborn
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that Manasseh was firstborn, yet Israel deliberately placed his right hand on Ephraim.

challenge.question: What does the image “the God which fed me all my life long” express?
answers: That God taught Israel to care for sheep
That God watched over, led, and cared for Israel throughout his life
That Israel worked as a shepherd when young
challenge.explanation: The image describes God as one who protected, guided, and cared for Israel throughout his life.

challenge.question: What does “let them grow into a multitude” mean at the end of the blessing?
answers: That the boys would learn to fish
That the boys would live near the sea
That their descendants would become very numerous
challenge.explanation: The blessing speaks of the descendants multiplying greatly.

questions.question: What can we infer from Israel placing his right hand on the younger Ephraim?
answers: The greater blessing was given to the younger, although Manasseh was firstborn
Ephraim was Manasseh’s father
Israel did not know who was firstborn
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that Manasseh was firstborn, yet Israel deliberately placed his right hand on Ephraim.

questions.question: What does the image “the God which fed me all my life long” express?
answers: That God taught Israel to care for sheep
That God watched over, led, and cared for Israel throughout his life
That Israel worked as a shepherd when young
questions.explanation: The image describes God as one who protected, guided, and cared for Israel throughout his life.

questions.question: What does “let them grow into a multitude” mean at the end of the blessing?
answers: That the boys would learn to fish
That the boys would live near the sea
That their descendants would become very numerous
questions.explanation: The blessing speaks of the descendants multiplying greatly.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Gives Ephraim Precedence over Manasseh

easy.question: On whose head did Jacob place his right hand?
answers: Ephraim
Manasseh
Joseph
easy.explanation: Jacob placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head.

easy.question: Who tried to move his father’s hand from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s?
answers: Manasseh
Jacob
Joseph
easy.explanation: Joseph saw what happened and tried to move his father’s hand from Ephraim to Manasseh.

easy.question: Who was firstborn among Ephraim and Manasseh?
answers: Ephraim
Manasseh
They were twins
easy.explanation: Joseph said of Manasseh, “This is the firstborn.”

medium.question: Why did Joseph think Jacob was making a mistake with his hands?
answers: Because Manasseh was the firstborn
Because Ephraim was not his son
Because Jacob did not know the young men
medium.explanation: Joseph thought the greater blessing should be placed on Manasseh, the firstborn.

medium.question: What did Jacob mean when he refused to move his hands?
answers: He agreed immediately
He would not consent to the change
He called for Joseph
medium.explanation: Jacob did not agree to change the position of his hands.

medium.question: What did Jacob say about Ephraim even though he was younger?
answers: That he would not become a people
That he would become greater than Manasseh
That he would receive only Manasseh’s blessing
medium.explanation: Jacob said that Ephraim, the younger brother, would be greater and that his descendants would become a multitude of nations.

challenge.question: What change in order was made at the end of the passage?
answers: Ephraim was placed before Manasseh
Manasseh was placed before Ephraim
They were placed in the same position
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly says that Jacob set Ephraim before Manasseh.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Jacob saying, “I know it, my son, I know it”?
answers: He had not heard Joseph
He understood the order of the sons and chose it deliberately
He had forgotten which son was firstborn
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that Jacob knew the facts and acted intentionally.

challenge.question: What central idea is emphasized by the younger Ephraim receiving precedence over the firstborn Manasseh?
answers: Birth order always determines the blessing
Joseph determined the order of the blessing
Blessing and destiny are not determined only by birth order
challenge.explanation: Jacob’s action shows that future status and blessing do not always depend on being born first.

questions.question: What change in order was made at the end of the passage?
answers: Ephraim was placed before Manasseh
Manasseh was placed before Ephraim
They were placed in the same position
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says that Jacob set Ephraim before Manasseh.

questions.question: What can we infer from Jacob saying, “I know it, my son, I know it”?
answers: He had not heard Joseph
He understood the order of the sons and chose it deliberately
He had forgotten which son was firstborn
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that Jacob knew the facts and acted intentionally.

questions.question: What central idea is emphasized by the younger Ephraim receiving precedence over the firstborn Manasseh?
answers: Birth order always determines the blessing
Joseph determined the order of the blessing
Blessing and destiny are not determined only by birth order
questions.explanation: Jacob’s action shows that future status and blessing do not always depend on being born first.

paragraphs.title: Jacob’s Farewell Words and Gift to Joseph

easy.question: To whom did Israel speak in these verses?
answers: Joseph
Moses
Abraham
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Israel said unto Joseph.”

easy.question: What did Israel promise that God would do?
answers: Give them a king
Bring them again to the land of their fathers
Build them a city
easy.explanation: Israel said that God would bring them again to the land of their fathers.

easy.question: What did Israel give Joseph?
answers: A special garment
A sword and bow
One portion above his brothers
easy.explanation: Israel told Joseph, “I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren.”

medium.question: What is the connection between Israel’s death and his words about God?
answers: Although Israel would die, he promised that God would remain with his descendants
Israel said that God would die with him
Israel asked Joseph to replace God
medium.explanation: Israel said, “I die,” and then added that God would be with them.

medium.question: What does “one portion above thy brethren” mean?
answers: One shoulder
An additional share or special portion
The name of a weapon
medium.explanation: In the context of Joseph receiving a gift above his brothers, it means an additional or special portion.

medium.question: What was the order of events described in the verses?
answers: God brought the people to the land, and then Israel died
Israel gave Joseph the portion, and then Joseph was born
Israel announced his death and God’s promise, and then mentioned Joseph’s special portion
medium.explanation: First Israel spoke of his death and God’s promise; afterward he mentioned what he had given Joseph.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the plural word “you” in the promise that God would bring “you” again?
answers: The promise concerned Joseph and his descendants, not only one person
The promise was only for Israel himself
The promise concerned only the Amorites
challenge.explanation: The plural wording shows that the promise concerned Joseph and his family or descendants.

challenge.question: What does “above thy brethren” mean in the context of Joseph’s gift?
answers: Joseph received the same portion as his brothers
Joseph received an advantage or an additional portion compared with his brothers
Joseph was commanded to fight his brothers
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that Joseph received an extra portion or special status compared with his brothers.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow” reveal about how Israel describes obtaining the place?
answers: The place was purchased from the Amorite with money
The place was given to Israel without any struggle
Israel describes obtaining it through armed conflict
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the sword and bow describes taking it from the Amorite through conflict or warfare.

questions.question: What can we infer from the plural word “you” in the promise that God would bring “you” again?
answers: The promise concerned Joseph and his descendants, not only one person
The promise was only for Israel himself
The promise concerned only the Amorites
questions.explanation: The plural wording shows that the promise concerned Joseph and his family or descendants.

questions.question: What does “above thy brethren” mean in the context of Joseph’s gift?
answers: Joseph received the same portion as his brothers
Joseph received an advantage or an additional portion compared with his brothers
Joseph was commanded to fight his brothers
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that Joseph received an extra portion or special status compared with his brothers.

questions.question: What does the phrase “which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow” reveal about how Israel describes obtaining the place?
answers: The place was purchased from the Amorite with money
The place was given to Israel without any struggle
Israel describes obtaining it through armed conflict
questions.explanation: Mentioning the sword and bow describes taking it from the Amorite through conflict or warfare.
